recipes.title: Apple Vinaigrette Slaw

ings.t: Carrots, julienned or finely grated (in place of cabbage)

steps: Whisk the vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon, olive oil, celery seed, salt and pepper until emulsified.
Combine the apples, carrots and scallions in a large bowl.
Toss with about two-thirds of the dressing. Add more only if needed; you want it lightly coated, not wet. Rest 20 to 30 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes:
You added mayo for creaminess. The other version in your notes uses honey, whole-grain plus Dijon mustard and garlic.
Original card used 3 cups green + 1 cup red cabbage; you swapped in carrots.
Dress only 20 to 30 minutes before serving so it stays crisp.

recipes.title: The Best Homemade Baked Mac and Cheese

ings.t: oz elbow macaroni (or other tubular pasta)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 3 or 4 quart baking dish. Toss the cheddar and Gruyère together in a bowl.
Cook the pasta about 1 minute short of al dente. Drain, toss with the olive oil and let it cool while you make the sauce.
Melt the 6 tbsp butter in a deep saucepan or Dutch oven. Whisk in the flour over medium heat for about 1 minute, until bubbly and golden.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cream until smooth. Once bubbles form on the surface, keep whisking 2 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Whisk in 2 cups of the cheese until smooth, then another 2 cups until creamy. The sauce should be thick.
Stir in the cooled pasta until fully coated.
Spread half the mac and cheese in the dish, sprinkle with the remaining 2 cups of cheese, then add the rest of the mac and cheese.
Mix the panko, Parmesan, melted butter and paprika and sprinkle over the top. Bake about 30 minutes, until bubbly and golden. Serve right away.
recipes.notes:
Shred block cheese yourself; pre-shredded doesn't melt as smoothly.
Cold milk into the roux keeps it from clumping.
Make ahead: assemble without the topping, freeze up to 2 months, thaw overnight and bake a little longer.
The site doesn't list servings, so set them with Edit if you want scaling.

recipes.title: Classic Banana Pudding

ings.t: box instant vanilla pudding mix (3.4 oz)

steps: Beat the heavy cream with the vanilla to stiff peaks.
Whisk the condensed milk and cold water together. Add the pudding mix and whisk about 2 minutes until it starts to thicken.
Fold about two-thirds of the whipped cream into the pudding. Save the rest for the top.
In a trifle dish or 9x13, layer wafers, then bananas, then pudding. Repeat, ending with pudding.
Spread the reserved whipped cream on top, garnish with a few wafers and chill at least 4 hours.
recipes.notes: Overnight is ideal so the wafers soften. If making ahead, a little lemon juice on the banana slices slows browning.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Barbacoa

ings.t: lb beef chuck roast, cut into 3-inch chunks
Cilantro and lime wedges, to serve

steps: Add everything except the bay leaves to the slow cooker.
Toss gently with tongs, tuck in the bay leaves and cover.
Cook on low 8 to 9 hours or high 4 to 5 hours, until the beef shreds easily. If it doesn't, keep going.
Move the beef to a board and shred with two forks.
Return it to the pot and stir so it soaks up the juices. Serve with cilantro and lime.
recipes.notes: You also referenced Wholesome Yum's Chipotle copycat (wholesomeyum.com/recipes/copycat-chipotle-barbacoa-slow-cooker-low-carb-paleo/). Its twist: blend the broth, chipotles, garlic, vinegar, lime and spices into a smooth sauce first, then pour it over the beef.

recipes.title: Roommate's Creole Mac & Cheese

ings.t: Butter and flour, for the roux

steps: Cook the elbow pasta until just short of done.
Cook the green pepper, onion and garlic, then build a roux with butter and flour.
Whisk in the heavy cream and simmer until it thickens.
Melt in the gouda, Monterey Jack and blue cheese, and season with creole and cajun seasoning, salt and pepper.
Fold in the pasta.
recipes.notes: Still open: baked or stovetop, and whether there's a protein. Amounts unknown. The steps are a best guess at the order.

recipes.title: Honey Garlic Glazed Salmon
steps: Pat the salmon dry and season both sides with salt, pepper, smoked paprika and blackening seasoning if using.
Set the oven rack to the middle position and preheat the broiler.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet. Add the garlic, water, soy sauce, sriracha, honey and lemon juice and cook 30 seconds.
Add the salmon skin side down and cook 3 minutes, basting often with the sauce.
Broil on high 5 to 6 minutes, basting once halfway, until caramelized and 145°F inside. Keep it skin side down; don't flip.
Plate and spoon the remaining sauce over the top. Garnish with parsley.
recipes.notes: Fixes from last time: make the sauce over MEDIUM, not medium-high, in a large skillet, since the honey burns fast. Keep the rack in the middle. If it's still raw, lower the rack and give it 3 to 5 more minutes.

log.n: Didn't go well: sauce burned before the salmon went in, and the salmon stayed raw under the broiler.

recipes.title: Chicken Thigh Karaage Curry
recipes.sourceName: Karaage from Just One Cookbook + Japanese boxed curry

ings.t: bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch pieces
cup potato starch or cornstarch (about 1/2 cup for 10 thighs)
Lemon wedges and chopped scallion, to serve
Onion, carrot and potato, as the box directs

steps: Put the chicken in a zip-top bag. Mix the grated onion, ginger, garlic, egg yolk, sake, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt and pepper, pour it in and rub it into the chicken.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour, ideally 3 to 4.
Start the curry per the box: cook the onion, carrot and potato, add water, simmer until tender, then stir in the roux off the heat. Keep warm.
Heat the oil in a wok to about 338°F (170°C).
Pull the chicken from the marinade, toss quickly in potato starch and leave the coating a little uneven.
Fry in batches of 5 pieces or fewer for 90 seconds at 320 to 338°F. Rest on a rack 4 minutes.
Fry again at 356°F (180°C) for about 45 seconds until deep golden. Drain on the rack.
Serve the curry over rice with the karaage on top, plus lemon and scallion.
recipes.notes: Your combo: Just One Cookbook's karaage on top of Japanese boxed curry. Curry amounts follow whatever box you buy. The double fry is what keeps it crisp under the sauce.

recipes.title: No-Bake Lemon Pudding Dessert
recipes.sourceName: Your banana pudding base, reworked with Claude

ings.t: cups lemon pudding (instant mix, made with a little less milk than the box says)
cups whipped cream (from heavy cream), plus more for the top

steps: Make the lemon pudding with a little less milk than the box calls for so it sets thicker.
Fold the whipped cream and lemon zest into the pudding. Taste and add a splash of lemon juice if it needs more brightness.
Layer Nilla wafers, then pudding, then another layer of wafers and pudding.
Chill at least 2 hours.
Close to serving, top with more whipped cream and the raspberries.
recipes.notes:
Boxed lemon pudding tastes weak on its own. The zest is the fix.
Homemade whipped cream deflates, so add the top layer close to serving.

log.n: Box lemon flavor was weak; half a lemon of zest fixed it.

recipes.title: Maple Syrup BBQ Sauce
steps: Whisk the ketchup, maple syrup, vinegar, Worcestershire and Dijon in a small saucepan.
Stir in the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, cayenne and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then lower the heat and cook uncovered 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.
Cool. It thickens more as it sits. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
recipes.notes:
Shortcut you used for the party: Carolina Gold BBQ sauce plus dark maple syrup, added a tablespoon at a time. A dash of smoked paprika and Worcestershire gives it more body.
Bourbon or a chipotle in adobo are good twists.

recipes.title: Miso Glazed Salmon

ings.t: Green onions and sesame seeds, for garnish (optional)

steps: Season the salmon with salt and pepper.
Whisk the miso, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar and sesame oil until smooth. Set aside 1 tbsp for glazing.
Marinate the salmon in the rest of the sauce for 1 to 3 hours.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Put the salmon in an oven-safe skillet and discard the marinade. Bake 12 to 15 minutes until nearly cooked through.
Brush with the reserved glaze and broil on high 1 to 2 minutes, until the center reaches 125 to 130°F.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Bake-then-broil: the bake cooks it gently, the short broil caramelizes the glaze without burning.

recipes.title: Skillet Chicken Pot Pie

ings.t: tbsp butter, plus more for the dish
medium-large boneless skinless chicken breasts, in 1-inch pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt and cook until the onion is soft and lightly colored.
Stir in the thyme, then the chicken seasoned with salt and pepper. Cook until it starts to brown. Sprinkle in the flour and cook 1 more minute.
Pour in the broth and half-and-half. Simmer, stirring, until slightly thinner than you want the filling. Stir in the peas, take it off the heat, adjust seasoning and let it cool slightly.
Butter a 9-inch pie plate and line it with one crust.
Spoon in the filling. Brush the edges with egg, lay the second crust on top, seal, trim and crimp.
Brush the top with egg wash and cut a small vent in the center.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden. Rest 10 to 15 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Pulled Pork on Waffles

ings.t: Carolina Gold BBQ sauce mixed with dark maple syrup, or Maple Syrup BBQ Sauce

steps: Rub the pork all over with the sugar and salt.
Cook the pork until it shreds easily, then shred.
Make the slaw components ahead; dress them 20 to 30 minutes before serving.
Assemble: waffle, then pork, then slaw, then a drizzle of maple BBQ sauce.
recipes.notes:
Sugar-forward rub on purpose: the sauces bring their own salt.
13 lb raw gives about 8 to 9 lb cooked, around 30 to 35 portions at 3 to 4 oz with other meats out.
Your cook method wasn't recorded, so add it with Edit.
Korean-inspired idea for next time: gochujang-maple glaze, Kewpie mayo, sesame-ginger slaw, crispy kimchi.

recipes.title: Ranchero Sauce

ings.t: jalapeño, diced (half, or seeded, for less heat)

steps: Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium. Add the onion, tomatoes, jalapeño, chipotle, garlic, oregano and salt. Cook about 10 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the broth and cook 1 minute. Take it off the heat and stir in the cilantro and lime juice.
Blend with an immersion blender until nearly smooth but still a little textured.
Taste. If it's sharp, add the sugar.
Cool, then refrigerate up to a week or freeze up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Roommate's BBQ Sauce

ings.t: Yellow mustard, about 1/3 as much as the ketchup
Optional: hot sauce, bourbon, or apple cider vinegar

steps: Whisk everything together in a saucepan.
Simmer gently about 15 minutes, then taste and adjust the sweet, tang and heat.
recipes.notes: Only the ketchup-to-mustard ratio is known. Add amounts with Edit once you've dialed it in. The simmer steps are a standard method, not your roommate's.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Shaking Beef (Bò Lúc Lắc)

ings.t: lb boneless ribeye, cut into 1-inch cubes

steps: Toss the beef with the garlic, brown sugar, 3 tbsp soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce and pepper. Marinate at room temperature 30 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, vinegar and water. Add the onion rings and let them soak.
Arrange the watercress and tomatoes on a platter.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering. Sear half the beef, shaking the pan, 3 to 5 minutes until charred and medium rare. Repeat with the rest.
Pile the beef over the greens and top with the pickled onions and cilantro. Serve with rice.
recipes.notes: Sear in batches so the beef chars instead of steaming.

recipes.title: Soy-Ginger Salmon with Onions and Carrots
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with foil.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, ginger and garlic in a small bowl.
Toss the carrots and onion with the vegetable oil, spread on the pan and roast 12 minutes.
Nestle the salmon among the vegetables and brush generously with glaze, saving a little.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until the salmon flakes and hits 145°F, brushing with the rest of the glaze halfway.
Top with scallions and sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Carrots get a head start since they take longer. Serve over rice to soak up the sauce.

recipes.title: Spicy Vodka Sausage Rigatoni
recipes.sourceName: Built with Claude around a 32 oz jar of Carbone Spicy Vodka

ings.t: oz sliced pancetta, cut into small pieces
tbsp kosher salt, for the pasta water

steps: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery. Mince the garlic. Cut the pancetta into small squares and squeeze the sausage out of its casings. Put a large pot of water on to boil.
Put the pancetta in a cold, wide pan over medium heat. Cook until the fat renders and it's crisp, about 5 minutes for sliced. Scoop it out and leave the fat.
Turn the heat to medium-high. Press the sausage into a flat layer and leave it 3 to 4 minutes until dark and crusty, then break it up and brown all over. Scoop it out, leaving about 2 tbsp of fat.
Lower to medium. Cook the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt until soft and lightly golden, scraping up the browned bits. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Return the sausage. Stir in the vodka sauce and cream and simmer gently over medium-low about 10 minutes while the pasta cooks.
Salt the boiling water and cook the rigatoni 2 minutes short of the package time. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with a splash of pasta water over medium heat until the sauce clings, about 2 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in half the parmesan, the crisp pancetta and the butter if using. Taste before salting. Serve with the rest of the parmesan on top.
recipes.notes:
The Carbone Spicy Vodka label calls for 8 oz cream per 24 oz sauce, so 1 1/3 cups for the 32 oz jar. Start with 1 cup if you want it spicier.
Add the parmesan and basil off the heat.
If you only have 1 lb pasta, the extra sauce keeps 4 days or freezes.

log.n: Used 3 oz pancetta. It got smoky, so render on medium. Food-processor veggies went mushy; cook them longer to dry out.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Creamy White Chicken Chili

ings.t: lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, trimmed
cans Great Northern beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
cans diced green chiles (4 oz), one hot and one mild
can whole kernel corn (15 oz), drained
Toppings: jalapeños, avocado, sour cream, tortilla strips, Monterey Jack

steps: Put the chicken in the slow cooker and top with the salt, pepper, cumin, oregano, chili powder and cayenne.
Add the onion, garlic, beans, green chiles, corn, broth and cilantro. Stir.
Cover and cook on low 8 hours or high 3 to 4 hours.
Pull out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot.
Stir in the cream cheese and half and half. Cover and cook on high 15 minutes until creamy.
Stir well and serve with toppings.
recipes.notes:
Your version: added Baldom Sazon Liquido Ranchero and Goya Recaito cilantro base, which pushed it in a Caribbean/Latin direction.
The original page also has stovetop and Instant Pot directions.

recipes.title: White Chicken Chili (Cooking Classy)

ings.t: Chicken broth (save 1/4 cup for the bean purée)
Cannellini beans (1 cup puréed, the rest whole)
Toppings: Monterey Jack, avocado, tortilla chips

steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high.
Cook the onion 4 minutes, then the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the broth, chilies and spices, season with salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Simmer on medium-low 15 minutes.
Drain and rinse the beans. Purée 1 cup of them with 1/4 cup broth until nearly smooth.
Stir in the Neufchâtel, corn, whole beans and puréed beans. Simmer 5 to 10 minutes more.
Stir in the chicken, lime juice and cilantro. Serve with toppings.
recipes.notes:
Amounts didn't come through from the site, so check the original before you cook and add them with Edit.
The trick: puréed beans make it creamy without flour.
